objective: Fix the confirmed Agents functionality and usability failures using existing project-scoped MCP, provider-readiness, and session lifecycle seams.
closed_decisions: Keep the change inside existing React/CSS seams and reuse AgentMcpPanel plus checkAgentAvailabilityForRepo; add no dependency, service, backend command, provider protocol, or persistence layer.

The empty workspace describes open conversations, not backend activity. A saved starting/running journal record without a matching live session receives a factual non-live label rather than being described as currently running.
A missing AgentSession is not active. Preserve true live-session labels when a matching session exists.
Expose one clearly named, lazy project MCP configuration entry from the Agents home before launch. Require explicit project choice when necessary and avoid duplicate DOM IDs.

Agents quick launch performs the same cached readiness check used by the project launcher, disables known-unavailable providers, and visibly explains checking, unavailable, and retryable-unknown states.
Long journal diagnostics may remain visually ellipsized but their full bounded text must be programmatically available without putting private diagnostic content into a generic top-level page label.
Localize exited, cancelled/canceled, and waiting lifecycle labels consistently in the transcript status surface.
Preserve all existing live launch, saved transcript, MCP read-only, and resume behavior; keep the implementation minimal and accessible at 800 by 600.
forbidden_changes: Do not change Rust, bus contracts, generated files, provider configuration, workbench persistence, credentials, dependencies, manifests, lockfiles, native test harnesses, or Pumarejo.
Do not add a new provider framework, state store, modal system, settings route, or broad Agents redesign.
Do not delete or mutate saved user conversations, MCP profiles, or repository content.
Do not edit campaign, orchestration, roadmap, Jira, release, branch, commit, push, PR, or user-owned files outside the owned file list.

acceptance_criteria.description: The no-open-terminal state and saved journal lifecycle labels no longer contradict each other, missing live sessions are not active, and focused tests cover stale and genuinely live records.

Project MCP inventory/profile management is discoverable and usable from the Agents home without launching a provider, mounts lazily, remains project-attributed, and retains existing read-only behavior in saved transcripts.
Agents quick launch reflects the same provider readiness result as the Dashboard, prevents known-unavailable launch, and presents actionable checking, retry, or unavailable copy with focused tests.
The full bounded saved-session diagnostic remains available to pointer and assistive-technology users when its visual preview is truncated.
Exited, cancelled/canceled, and waiting transcript lifecycle states are localized consistently with focused regression coverage.
Focused ConsoleDockPanel and MCP tests plus the production frontend build pass without out-of-scope changes.
